name: Logical Connector Profiling
description: Analyzes the frequency and variety of transitional words (e.g., 'however', 'furthermore', 'therefore'). AI models tend to over-utilize explicit logical connectors to artificially structure their outputs, resulting in a predictable, highly formulaic argumentative rhythm.
algorithm: Discourse Marker Frequency and Variance Analysis
mechanism: This method parses the text to identify all discourse markers and logical connectors used to bridge sentences and paragraphs. It categorizes these connectors by function (additive, adversative, causal, sequential) and calculates their overall density relative to the text length. LLMs are trained heavily on structured, argumentative datasets and are tuned to produce 'helpful and clear' responses. As a result, they frequently rely on a rigid skeleton of transitional adverbs ('Firstly', 'Moreover', 'In conclusion', 'Thus') to forcefully signpost their logic. Human writers, even when drafting formal essays, use these explicit markers much more sparingly, often relying on implicit logical flow, narrative momentum, or more subtle structural shifts. The analyzer compares the ratio of explicit connectors to sentences against human baselines. If a text exhibits an unnatural density of textbook transition words, particularly at the beginning of every new sentence or paragraph, it generates a high probability score for AI authorship.
useCase: Highly effective for auditing academic papers, cover letters, and analytical reports where AI tends to expose itself through excessively rigid, 'five-paragraph essay' style transition framing.
strengths:
• Targets the LLM's fundamental alignment training, which prioritizes overt clarity and structured argumentation over organic pacing.
• Very fast to compute, as it relies on matching against comprehensive lexicons of discourse markers rather than complex semantic parsing.
• Highly interpretable; the specific overused connectors (like the notorious 'Furthermore') can be explicitly highlighted as evidence.
limitations:
• Susceptible to false positives in texts written by non-native speakers (ESL learners) or novice writers who are artificially taught to overuse transition words to structure their writing.
• Can be bypassed by prompt engineering (e.g., 'Write without using transition words like however or furthermore').
• Less effective on creative fiction or casual dialogue where LLMs naturally suppress formal connectors.
parameters:
Analysis: Discourse Marker Token Matching
Metric: Connector-to-Sentence Ratio and Lexical Variance of Connectors
Output: 0-100 Transition Rigidity Score
accuracy: Moderate to High — 72-84% accuracy. Acts as a strong complementary heuristic to highlight the stereotypical, overly-didactic tone of ChatGPT and Claude.

references.title: Jurafsky, D. & Martin, J.H. (2024). Speech and Language Processing. 3rd Edition.
Guo, B. et al. (2023). How Close is ChatGPT to Human Experts? Comparison Corpus, Evaluation, and Detection. NeurIPS.
